Subject: Follow-up: Model fit & quantization trade study

Tom / Aisha - thanks again for the time today. High-level recap + suggested next steps below:

Recap from discovery call:
- Primary goal: extractive & generative summarization for customer support transcripts (20k daily conversations).
- Latency target: P95 generation <= 350ms for 512-token responses; throughput: ~200 concurrent requests at peak.
- Quality priority: factual consistency & long-context coherence (>2k tokens).
- Constraints: budget-conscious (aiming to reduce per-token unit cost) and must pass data residency review for US-only logs.

Recommended evaluation plan (what we propose Redwood runs for you):
1) Model candidates: 7B and 13B open models we vetted (Llama-3-7B, Llama-3-13B, Mistral-7B-Med).
2) Compression/quantization matrix: AWQ 4-bit, GPTQ 4-bit (per-op variants), and baseline FP16/FP32.
3) Prompts & evals: run your prompt set (attached: finwave_promptset_v1.csv) plus a synthetic long-context suite (links in the Drive doc).
4) Metrics: ROUGE, BLEU, human eval for hallucination rate, latency P50/P95, and tokens/sec for throughput.

Quantization / throughput notes (tradeoffs):
- AWQ (our recommended starting point): generally best throughput/size tradeoff with smaller quality delta for many generator tasks vs GPTQ; tends to preserve attention behavior that matters for long-context coherence. Good starting point for 4-bit experiments.
- GPTQ: well-understood and sometimes slightly better for certain 7B models; requires per-model calibration and can be slower to iterate if we need multiple passes.
- FP8 (where supported): delivers excellent latency without extreme accuracy loss on smaller sequence lengths but is less mature across all kernels and hardware; higher risk for regressions on hallucination-sensitive workloads.

Suggested immediate next steps:
- I will spin up a Redwood evaluation run across the 7B/13B candidates with AWQ and GPTQ 4-bit configurations and share a short report in 5 business days.
- Please confirm the prompt set in the attachment is representative and send any additional edge cases.
- If you're aligned, we'll provision a dedicated eval pool in us-west for repeatability; Vivek (cc'd) will coordinate sandbox access and data ingestion.

Attachments: finwave_promptset_v1.csv, quant-trade-study-AWQ-vs-GPTQ.pdf (summary + benchmark methodology).

Thanks,

Tom - good questions; quick answers and a little more color:

1) Latency: For 13B on AWQ 4-bit we expect to be close to your P95 target at moderate concurrency on our Dedicated pool; at 200 concurrent requests you may see P95 creep to ~450ms depending on response length and KV-cache hit-rate. That's why we recommended testing both 7B and 13B - 7B AWQ typically meets the 350ms P95 comfortably while still improving quality vs smaller baselines.

2) Token cost delta: rough numbers (ballpark, depends on batch sizing/seq length):
- FP16 baseline: 1.0x cost
- 4-bit AWQ: ~0.25-0.35x cost
- 4-bit GPTQ: ~0.28-0.4x cost (varies by model and calibration)
These assume similar batching; intelligent batching and prefix caching can push numbers lower. We'll include a cost breakdown in the eval report.

3) US-only eval environment: Vivek - can you confirm we can provision a US-only sandbox with data residency controls and S3 ACLs limited to our US region? If so, we'll proceed to ingest the prompt set and edge cases Tom will send.

Next: I'm kicking off the AWQ + GPTQ runs on both 7B and 13B tonight. I'll attach the benchmark baseline and a short runbook for the evals in the Drive link.

Cheers,
Marissa
